disruption_scenario: Supplier X has delayed shipment of 5,000 units of Widget-A by 10 days due to port congestion.

blackboard_evolution.content: SUP-201 shipment delayed by 10 days due to port congestion; 5,000 units of Widget-A affected.
Projected demand over 10-day delay: 2,912 units of Widget-A.
Current inventory: 3,200 units. Demand: 2,912 units. Projected buffer remaining: 288 units. Shortfall = 0 units. Stock is SUFFICIENT.
Backup vendors evaluated: Vertex Logistics (lead time 6 days, premium 12%), Anchor Bay (lead time 8 days, premium 8%).
Wait option cost delta: $0.00. Vertex expedited backup: $14,400 for 1,200 units.
A2A Audit completed: Vulnerability Index 60/100 (ELEVATED). ISO 9001 certified: True. Recommendation: Buffer sufficient; maintain daily port clearance monitoring.

structured_decision.recommended_action: Wait out delay with conditional backup order
structured_decision.justification: On-hand inventory of 3,200 units comfortably covers the 10-day demand forecast of 2,912 units. A buffer of 288 units remains, resulting in zero shortfall. Defaulting to wait avoids unnecessary premium supplier switching costs while original shipment remains in transit.

options_evaluated.pros: Zero incremental cost delta; existing inventory avoids assembly disruption
options_evaluated.cons: Buffer margin tight at 288 units if port delay extends beyond 10 days
Creates 5,000 unit overstock risk once original shipment clears customs
